routes.description: Establish that divine simplicity follows from classical commitments concerning aseity and pure actuality, then explain apparent plurality, Trinitarian relations, freedom, and contingent knowledge without introducing real intrinsic composition or change in God.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its account excludes intrinsic parts on principled metaphysical grounds while preserving intelligible divine attributes, real Trinitarian relational distinction, free creation or noncreation, and omniscient knowledge of contingent and changing reality.

motionBridge.description: Show that one intrinsically simple divine reality can satisfy the classical-theist, Trinitarian, freedom, and omniscience commitments named in the motion.

centralBridges.description: Derive the exclusion of intrinsic composition from aseity, explanatory independence, or the pure actuality required of a first cause.
Distinguish real intrinsic composition from grounded conceptual distinctions, analogical predication, and extrinsic creature-directed predications.
Explain how persons and opposed procession-relations can be identical with the divine essence without becoming additional intrinsic constituents.
Explain contingent and temporally varying knowledge attributions through an immutable divine intellect and causal efficacy together with extrinsic truths and creaturely changes.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Treat distinct alleged forms of composition separately while identifying the act-potency principles that connect them.
Account for creation and noncreation as free possibilities that neither complete nor intrinsically improve God.

routes.description: Define the intrinsic distinctions prohibited by simplicity and show that classical theism's positive commitments generate at least one such distinction through dependence, Trinitarian processions, free contingent knowledge, or knowledge of changing reality.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the proposed reconciliations cannot preserve the relevant Trinitarian or epistemic realities without admitting a positive intrinsic distinction, contingent state, potentiality, or change inconsistent with divine simplicity.

motionBridge.description: Show that the commitments named in the motion require distinctions or changes that an intrinsically partless God cannot coherently possess.

centralBridges.description: Specify which positive ontological items or distinctions count as intrinsic constituents and why simplicity excludes them.
Show that divine independence can be understood without eliminating every intrinsic distinction, undermining the inference from aseity to simplicity.
Show that real processions, opposed relations, or asymmetric personal predicates require distinctions not reducible to the undifferentiated divine essence.
Show that free noncreation or changing contingent truths require contingent intrinsic knowledge or epistemic change incompatible with immutability and pure actuality.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require an account of what divine knowledge consists in if its contingent differentiation is assigned wholly or principally to extrinsic reality.
Establish the availability of an alone world through divine freedom, self-sufficiency, or reasons compatible with refraining from creation.

sections.title: Metaphysical content, parts, and divine predication
sections.rationale: This issue fixes what simplicity excludes and whether conceptual, analogical, relational, or truthmaker-based distinctions preserve meaningful divine attributes without adding positive intrinsic constituents.

sections.title: Aseity, pure actuality, and the exclusion of composition
sections.rationale: This issue tests the principal positive grounds for simplicity and the counterclaim that divine independence can survive intrinsic multiplicity under alternative accounts of dependence, grounding, and unity.

sections.title: Trinitarian persons, processions, and subsistent relations
sections.rationale: This issue directly addresses whether real personal and procession-based distinctions can be identical with one divine essence or instead constitute intrinsic plurality prohibited by simplicity.

sections.title: Divine freedom and knowledge of contingent, changing reality
sections.rationale: This issue joins the creationless-world and changing-truth objections with accounts of extrinsic predication, immutable intellect, causality, and creaturely relations, covering the motion's central freedom and omniscience requirements.
